name: ClinPGx / PharmGKB
scope: Annotations linking variants, genes and drugs: variant annotations (4.1 MB zip), relationships (4.1 MB), summary annotations (1.2 MB), clinical guideline annotations, drug labels, pathways.
mapping_methods: rsID- and haplotype-level; coordinates must be mapped separately.

quantitative.summary: Evidence levels and categorical annotations; some effect sizes in variant annotations.

licence.name: CC BY-SA 4.0 (data usage policy)
licence.redistribution: Share-alike and attribution required for redistribution

known_omissions: Structural/copy-number haplotypes (e.g. CYP2D6 duplications) need PharmVar/CPIC definitions

reuse_decision.rationale: Small archives; Open Targets only carries a pharmacogenomics subset.

mechanism_evidence.note: variant-drug annotations with levels of evidence

components.name: variant and clinical annotations from the literature

evidence_profile.biological_context: Annotations linking variants, haplotypes, genes and drugs from published studies. Each annotation records the studied variant or haplotype, the drug, a phenotype category, the population and a level of evidence.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Literature-derived annotations with levels of evidence for clinical annotations. Individual studies are small and often conflict, and the annotation level is not an effect size.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate. Relationships state an association between genotype and drug response; molecular mechanism is annotated only where the study reports it.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Drug-specific response phenotypes (efficacy, toxicity, dosage) in studied populations; not transferable across drugs or ancestries without evidence.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No annotation means no curated study for that variant-drug pair and not that genotype is irrelevant; rare variants and alleles outside the studied panels have no annotation.

overlaps_with_sources.note: ClinPGx comprises PharmGKB, CPIC and PharmCAT; clinical guideline annotations include CPIC guidelines, so count a guideline once
